keyVerseText: And his servant Zimri, captain of half his chariots, conspired against him, as he was in Tirzah, drinking himself drunk in the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah. steward: Heb. which was over
rootMeaning: The root of אַרְצָא (ʼartsâʼ) is אֶרֶץ (ʼerets), which fundamentally means earth, land, or ground. The etymology indicates a sense of 'earthiness,' suggesting something grounded or connected to the earth. While אֶרֶץ broadly refers to the physical earth or land, אַרְצָא as a proper name carries this earthy connotation, emphasizing a tangible, concrete identity rather than an abstract concept.
usageInScripture: This word appears only once in Scripture, specifically as a proper name referring to a man who was steward or chamberlain to King Elah of Israel. The top translation reflects this personal name usage, 'of Arza,' rather than a common noun. This singular occurrence highlights that while the root word relates to earth or land, this form is specialized as a personal designation within the historical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding אַרְצָא as a name derived from the concept of 'earthiness' reminds us that biblical names often carry deep significance rooted in creation and God's sovereign ordering of the world. Even a servant or steward like Arza, whose name links to the earth, reflects the grounding of human roles within God's created order. This connection underscores the biblical theme that all human authority and service exist under God's sovereign rule over the earth. It also invites reflection on how God uses ordinary, earthly individuals to fulfill His divine purposes in history.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 16:9, the mention of 'the house of Arza steward of his house in Tirzah' situates the narrative within a specific earthly and historical context. The word אַרְצָא here identifies a real person entrusted with responsibility, grounding the story in tangible human relationships and duties. This highlights the reality of human agency and the earthly setting in which divine providence unfolds, as Zimri conspires while in the steward's house.
